legend.R: raised ground (plateau, one or more blocks above G)

focal.what: The central black pupil and electric-green corona monument

composition.mass: Visual weight rests heavily in the centre-left mass formed by the ivory sclera ground and the raised blue iris dome.
composition.read: The viewer enters from the low pale sclera plane on the west, advances toward the elevated stepped iris disc and central pupil monument, and follows the curving planetary ring path sweeping out into the dark southeastern expanse. The dark frame of eyelash blades and space void binds the composition.

lighting.notes: stellar ignition flare in deep space vacuum: Reflects the intense, sharp contrast between the pitch-black cosmos (#14120b) and the crisp white-blue flare at the iris edge as noted in ANALYSIS.palette.value_structure.

rules: Place eyelash-blade props strictly along the northern and southern perimeter ridges.
Keep the central 2x2 F cell reserved for the pupil-singularity.
Scatter asteroid-boulder props exclusively across the southeastern accretion ring path.
Place nebula-cluster masses on the elevated northeastern corner plateau.

lens.aspect: Airbrush gradients, frisket stencil borders, and ink liner brushwork from ANALYSIS.medium
lens.place: An astronomical observatory disc sculpted from lacquered airbrush pigments and cosmic debris
lens.summary: A cosmic eye rendered as a tiered disc of atomized pigment rings floating in deep space lacquer.
lens.differs: Unlike a biological landscape or an architectural sanctum, this level is structured around concentric airbrush gradients that step downward from a central pupil into an orbital accretion ring.

concept.name: lens-medium
concept.fragment: LENS "medium": the artwork's MATERIAL AND MARKS become the island's physical character. Start from ANALYSIS.medium and ANALYSIS.palette, not from the subject. The ground is made of the marks: single-stroke ink becomes ribbon land and sweeping arcs of path with void where the paper is empty (shaper "ribbon", or "spiral" for a curl); airbrush gradients become soft radial terraces fading outward (shaper "radial"); fauvist or knife strokes become a patchwork of flat colour blocks at different heights (shaper "patchwork"); charcoal smudge becomes soft-edged dark masses with pale mist lying in the hollows (shaper "mound" or "basin"); pencil hatching or scratchy ink becomes angular slabs split by thin seams (shaper "shards"); vector doodles become dense small ornament on a tidy mirrored plan (shaper "symmetric"). Choose shaper params from the marks themselves (how many strokes, how wide, which way they sweep, how many blocks). Palette, surface_mix and cliff_treatment follow the medium (ink: paper-pale sand and ink-dark cliffs; airbrush: rings of surfaces fading by value; fauvist: saturated patches; charcoal: soft grey-green, mossy or soft cliffs). New props are the marks made solid: a brush flick as a curved blade of stone, a smudge as a low soft boulder, a doodle as a ring of beads, a knife stroke as a flat tilted slab. The figure's pose comes from how it is drawn (a single continuous stroke, a stack of colour patches), and it may be a monument of the marks rather than a living creature.
